read.thesis: AWS grew 28% to $37.6B with a $364B backlog excluding a >$100B Anthropic deal, but Q1 cash capex of $43.2B and rising memory costs weigh on near-term free cash flow.

capex.quote: the faster AWS grows, the more short-term CapEx we will spend

triggers.label: AWS growth 28% YoY
triggers.quote: growth accelerated 480 basis points to 28% year over year

triggers.label: Backlog $364B ex-Anthropic
triggers.quote: the backlog for Q1 is $364 billion. That does not include the recent deal that we announced with Anthropic for over $100 billion.

triggers.label: Cash capex $43.2B in Q1
triggers.quote: Our cash CapEx is $43.2 billion in Q1.

triggers.label: Memory costs skyrocketed
triggers.quote: the cost of components, particularly memory, has skyrocketed

triggers.label: Trainium commitments >$225B
triggers.quote: we now have over $225 billion in revenue commitments for Trainium

guidance.quote: Q2 net sales are expected to be between $194 billion and $199 billion.
Q2 operating income is expected to be between $20 billion and $24 billion.
we do expect a year-over-year cost increase of approximately $1 billion related to Amazon LEO

red_flags.label: Early-year FCF challenged by capex
red_flags.quote: the early years’ free cash flow is challenged until these initial tranches of capacity are being monetized

red_flags.label: Memory supply tightness
red_flags.quote: there is just not enough capacity for the amount of demand

evasions.quote: So I do not have a new update on capital.
